validation.notes: Repaired packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts in two places. (1) loadEntriesFromFile(): the parsed final newline-less record (finalEntry) was computed and discarded, so resuming a session dropped its tail while the file was still repaired with appendFileSync('\n'); the record is now pushed before the header validation so it is retained exactly once, malformed fragments are still ignored, non-session files are still left untouched, and the single newline repair plus a later append no longer merge records. (2) migrateV1ToV2(): the collision-check Set passed to generateId() was never populated, so a duplicate generator result produced duplicate entry ids and a broken parent chain; minted ids are now recorded so generateId() retries. .prale-eval/regression.mjs links the real modules session-manager.ts, core/messages.ts and utils/paths.ts via subject.mjs createGraph and supplies its own boundary fakes (config exports, pi-ai uuidv7/getCurrentSystemMessage, child-process spawnProcessSync, a scripted crypto.randomUUID, and a fixed Date clock inside the module graph), so no real time or randomness is correctness evidence; temp files live in .prale-eval/tmp and are removed by the script. It asserts: tail record retained exactly once plus one appended newline; idempotent re-read with unchanged bytes; malformed-line skipping; ordered Unicode payloads; resume repairs the tail before appending so the next record stays parseable; a colliding batch transfer fails without touching the colliding source or the existing destination bytes while later transfers still run and retain the unterminated tail exactly once; legacy migration keeps unique ids and valid parents under a colliding id generator. Verified detection by restoring each defect alone: dropped finalEntry push fails at 'the unterminated final record must not be dropped' (2 !== 3) and missing ids.add() fails at 'colliding ids must be retried' (1 !== 2), both as plain node:assert/strict failures rather than crashes or import errors. Limitation: vitest and the repository's other Node dependencies are not installed in this workspace, so the repository's own TypeScript tests (e.g. packages/coding-agent/test/session-manager/file-operations.test.ts) could not be executed; they cover the same expectations behaviourally.
